title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1970 work on Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) groups and Dieudonné crystals, specifically the deformation-theoretic (Grothendieck–Messing) treatment of Lubin–Tate formal groups. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: they are typescript pages of the Bourbaki fascicule on manifolds, reused as scrap paper.

Setup, as far as it can be reconstructed. A is the ring of integers of a finite extension K of Q_p, with residue field k. The ring Ω acting on the group appears to be the same ring as A: the page writes Ω̌⊗A as obtained from Ω̌ via λ↦λ⊗1 : A→A⊗A, which only makes sense if Ω = A. Then Ω̌ = Hom_{Z_p}(Ω, Z_p) is the inverse different, viewed as an invertible Ω-module. G is a p-divisible (formal) group over A with an Ω-action (a formal Ω-module), and G* is its Serre dual.

The Dieudonné crystal evaluated on A gives M_A. It is free of rank one over Ω⊗_{Z_p}A, and its dual M̌ is ≃ Ω̌⊗_{Z_p}A. It carries the Hodge filtration 0→ω_G→M_A→t_{G*}→0, called (*), together with its dual sequence (**).

Argument on the page.
- Both t_G and Ω̌⊗_{Z_p}A are rank-one modules over A⊗_{Z_p}A.
- The strictness condition says that Ω acts on Lie G through the structure map.
- The multiplication map p_0 : A⊗A→A is surjective.
- Hence t_G is the base change of Ω̌⊗_{Z_p}A along p_0. Since Ω̌⊗A is itself the base change of Ω̌ along λ↦λ⊗1, one gets canonically t_G ≃ Ω̌, equivalently ω_G ≃ Ω.
- Then (**) is the dual of (*), and the canonical filtrations coincide with those induced from M_A⊗_A k.
- By the Grothendieck–Messing classification (deformations correspond to lifts of the Hodge filtration), this verifies the Lubin–Tate existence and uniqueness theorem. Grothendieck notes it comes out in a weaker form as regards uniqueness, and under an extra hypothesis: the existence of a 'distinguished point'. This may refer to a choice of uniformizer or Frobenius lift; the reading is unsure.

Dropping that hypothesis, he works rationally, over K. The classification of deformations gives canonical exact sequences:
- 0→ω_G⊗_A K→M_K→t_{G*}⊗K→0, with M_K ≃ Ω̌⊗_{Z_p}K;
- 0→ω_{G*}⊗K→M̌_K→t_G⊗K→0.
The quotient is then t_G⊗K ≃ M̌_K ⊗_{Ω⊗K} (K⊗K, p_0) ≃ Ω̌⊗K.

The point is that Ω⊗_{Z_p}K = K⊗_{Q_p}K splits as a product of fields indexed by the embeddings. The rational Hodge filtration of a Lubin–Tate group is therefore the eigenline cut out by the multiplication (identity-embedding) factor. This is the standard 'Hodge type' description of Lubin–Tate groups: one embedding of weight 1, all others of weight 0.
errors: The final expression 'Ω̌⊗_A K' only makes sense if Ω = A, or it should read Ω̌⊗_Ω K; this is notational looseness.
The subscript of the base change in the last formula reads Ω̌⊗_{Z_p}K in the image, but the ring acting should be Ω⊗_{Z_p}K = K⊗K; this is a slip.

Uniqueness is acknowledged by Grothendieck himself to come out weaker than in Lubin–Tate, and the argument uses an extra hypothesis ('point distingué'). These are not errors, but the argument is incomplete as written.

ideas.what: Proof of Lubin–Tate existence/uniqueness via crystalline Dieudonné theory: deformations of a formal Ω-module correspond to Ω-stable lifts of the Hodge filtration in the rank-one Ω⊗A-module M
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory applied to Lubin–Tate / strict formal O-modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1970 ICM, Montréal 1970 lectures), Messing (1972); later Drinfeld (1974) and Gross–Hopkins for O-module versions
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970/1974); ICM Nice 1970 address 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux'

ideas.what: Canonical identification t_G ≃ Ω̌ (inverse different), ω_G ≃ Ω, obtained by base change along the multiplication map A⊗A→A
ideas.modern_name: Lie algebra of a strict formal O-module; appearance of the different in Hodge–Tate/de Rham comparison for Lubin–Tate groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Lubin–Tate; different-theoretic statements in Fontaine (1982, 'Formes différentielles et modules de Tate') and in work on Lubin–Tate duality

ideas.what: Rational Hodge filtration of a Lubin–Tate group: M_K free of rank one over K⊗_{Q_p}K, with t_G⊗K the factor cut out by multiplication p_0
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration / Hodge–Tate weights of Lubin–Tate characters (weight 1 at the identity embedding, 0 elsewhere); Gross–Hopkins period map picture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine, Gross–Hopkins, Colmez (Lubin–Tate characters as crystalline characters)

missed.claim: An early (c.1970) crystalline re-derivation of the Lubin–Tate theorem, including the K⊗K eigenspace description of the Hodge filtration. This anticipates the later standard p-adic Hodge-theoretic description of Lubin–Tate characters. It is historically interesting, but the mathematics is now standard.
missed.quote: on a vérifié ... le th. d'existence et d'unicité de Lubin-Tate, ... sous l'hyp. complémentaire que ∃ point dist.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence that Grothendieck tested his crystalline Dieudonné theory on Lubin–Tate groups. It does not add new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a sketch, in Grothendieck's own hand, of Lubin–Tate via Dieudonné crystals and deformation theory. That is a natural test case of his 1970 theory and was later carried out in the literature (Messing, Drinfeld, Gross–Hopkins). It is of mild historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 probably reads 'sont de rang 1 sur A⊗_{Z_p}A' (both are rank-one modules over A⊗A) rather than '1 [?] sur A vers A⊗A'.
'p est surjectif' is likely 'p_0 est surjectif' (the multiplication A⊗A→A).
In the last formula the base-change subscript is written Ω̌⊗_{Z_p}K in the image; the ring intended is Ω⊗_{Z_p}K = K⊗K.
The hypothesis line reads roughly '∃ point dist. sur k̄A / πA' and is uncertain; 'dist.' = 'distingué'.
'mentionnée plus haut' is probably the intended reading in 'classification des déformations, ... plus [?]'.
The neighbouring pages are typescript Bourbaki pages (Variétés différentielles, n° 382) on the verso, unrelated to this manuscript.
